claim: A KDP paperback cover file is only the right size for one page count. A 6 x 9 in book on white paper needs a full cover 12.520 in wide at 120 pages, 12.588 in at 150 pages and 12.700 in at 200 pages, 9.250 in tall each time, because the spine goes from 0.270 in to 0.338 in to 0.450 in. Add or cut pages after the cover is made and the cover has to be resized. KDP's help says: "If the file is sized at dimensions other than those expected, Print Previewer will note the discrepancy and prevent approval."
notes: Real-time capture of the live free spine calculator at 360x640 CSS px, 3x device pixels, held on one frame for the whole clip: Trim size (6 x 9 in), Page count, Paper (Black & white on white paper), then the two answers, 'Spine width' with its millimetre line and 'Full cover PDF size' with its millimetre line; the top of the 'Design canvas at 300 dpi' box shows at the bottom edge. The first label, 'Trim size', sits 90 px down in the 1080x1920 video, clear of a 78 px top bar. Order: 120 pages (spine 0.270 in / 6.9 mm; cover 12.520 x 9.250 in / 318.0 x 234.9 mm) for about 4 s, then 150 typed into Page count (spine 0.338 in / 8.6 mm; cover 12.588 x 9.250 in / 319.7 x 234.9 mm), then 200 typed (spine 0.450 in / 11.4 mm; cover 12.700 x 9.250 in / 322.6 x 234.9 mm). The grey ring marks each tap on the Page count box. Only the page count changes; trim and paper stay as they are. The 200-page result holds still for about 6 s at the end for the end card. Where the figures come from: KDP's cover page (the second backing link) gives white paper as 0.002252 in a page, so 120 x 0.002252 = 0.270, 150 x 0.002252 = 0.338 and 200 x 0.002252 = 0.450; cover width = bleed + back + spine + front + bleed (0.125 + 6 + spine + 6 + 0.125); cover height = 9 + 0.25. So 30 more pages make the cover 0.068 in wider and 80 more make it 0.180 in wider. KDP's own cover calculator, asked on 2026-11-14 for a 6 x 9 in paperback, black and white on white paper, returns the same: full cover 12.52 x 9.25 with spine 0.27 at 120 pages, 12.588 x 9.25 with spine 0.338 at 150, and 12.7 x 9.25 with spine 0.45 at 200. The quoted sentence is from KDP's 'Fix Paperback and Hardcover Formatting Issues' page (the third backing link), under 'Cover size', read on 2026-11-14. Caveats, and the first one matters most: KDP's page gives no tolerance, so it does not say how small a difference is let through, and we have not put a wrong-sized cover through KDP's Print Previewer ourselves; the claim is what size KDP expects and what its help page says happens, not a test of our own. The front and back covers do not change, only the spine between them, so in practice the art is moved apart, not redrawn. These are white-paper figures; cream paper is 0.0025 in a page, so the same 30 pages add 0.075 in there. While a number is half typed the calculator shows, for about a fifth of a second, the figures for KDP's 24-page minimum (0.054 in and 12.304 x 9.250 in): those frames are not a result. The pixel size at 300 dpi (3756, 3776 and 3810 px wide by 2775) is partly cut off at the bottom of the frame and is not part of the claim. If a caption sits over the spine figure, the millimetre line under it (6.9, 8.6, 11.4 mm) is the spine width, not the change in the cover. Puzzle Press itself makes puzzle books; the calculator is free and works for any paperback. No tint or mark added.
